description_good_justification: The README opens with what Bientôt does: a Windows notification-area app that tells you whether you will finish the day's work before the time you want to leave. https://github.com/Thanaen/Bientot#readme
interact_justification: The README explains how to download the app, and CONTRIBUTING.md how to report bugs, propose ideas and send pull requests. https://github.com/Thanaen/Bientot/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_justification: https://github.com/Thanaen/Bientot/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md describes the contribution process: issue first for larger changes, pull requests, required checks, squash merge.
contribution_requirements_justification: https://github.com/Thanaen/Bientot/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md lists the coding, commit, test and localization requirements, and the pull request template repeats the checks.
floss_license_osi_justification: The MIT license is approved by the OSI.
documentation_basics_justification: The README covers what the app does, how to install it and how to use it; docs/ holds troubleshooting, privacy and architecture notes. https://github.com/Thanaen/Bientot/tree/main/docs
documentation_interface_justification: Bientôt is a desktop app: the README documents its interface, docs/privacy.md lists every file it stores and every request it sends, and docs/troubleshooting.md covers common problems, updates and diagnostics. https://github.com/Thanaen/Bientot/blob/main/docs/privacy.md
sites_https_justification: The project site https://bientot.dev, the repository and the downloads (GitHub releases, Microsoft Store) are all served over HTTPS.
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests: searchable, addressable by URL, open to anyone with a GitHub account, no proprietary client needed. https://github.com/Thanaen/Bientot/issues
english_justification: Documentation, code, commits and the issue tracker are in English; reports in French are accepted too.
maintained_justification: Active development with several merged pull requests and releases per week.
repo_track_justification: Git records who changed what and when.
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands on main through a pull request, between releases.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique version (1.0.<commit count>) and a matching Git tag. https://github.com/Thanaen/Bientot/releases
version_semver_justification: Versions follow the MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH format of Semantic Versioning.
version_tags_justification: Each release is tagged v<version> in Git.
release_notes_justification: Each GitHub release carries human-readable notes listing the user-visible changes (scripts/release-notes.sh). https://github.com/Thanaen/Bientot/releases
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability has been fixed in Bientôt so far. When one is, its release notes will name it.
report_process_justification: Bugs and ideas go through the GitHub issue forms. https://github.com/Thanaen/Bientot/issues/new/choose
report_responses_justification: Bug reports are answered or turned into pull requests, usually within days. https://github.com/Thanaen/Bientot/issues?q=is%3Aissue
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are answered in their issue and tracked with labels and milestones.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports go through GitHub private vulnerability reporting, as SECURITY.md explains. https://github.com/Thanaen/Bientot/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md commits to a first answer within a week.
build_justification: Cargo builds the app (cargo build), and CONTRIBUTING.md documents the commands.
build_floss_tools_justification: Rust, Cargo and Bun are free software.
test_justification: The Cargo workspace has unit and integration tests, and the web service has Bun tests; both are released under the MIT license with the code.
test_invocation_justification: cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked, and bun test for the web service, as documented in CONTRIBUTING.md.
test_most_justification: The domain, storage and core crates are covered by unit, fixture and fuzz tests; Windows-only code is tested on a Windows CI runner.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs the tests on every pull request and push to main. https://github.com/Thanaen/Bientot/actions/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md and the project constitution require automated tests with new features and bug fixes. https://github.com/Thanaen/Bientot/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#commits-and-pull-requests
tests_are_added_justification: Recent feature and fix pull requests add tests alongside the code. https://github.com/Thanaen/Bientot/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md and the pull request template ask for tests and list the commands to run.
warnings_justification: CI runs cargo clippy on all targets and TypeScript in strict mode.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any clippy warning (-D warnings), so none reaches main.
warnings_strict_justification: Warnings are errors in CI (cargo clippy -- -D warnings), on Linux and for the Windows target.
delivery_mitm_justification: The app is delivered through the Microsoft Store (signed by Microsoft) and GitHub releases over HTTPS, with SLSA provenance attestations; updates are fetched over HTTPS.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is ever retrieved over plain HTTP: release metadata and packages are fetched over HTTPS only.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: Dependabot, OSV-Scanner (through OpenSSF Scorecard) and CodeQL report no open vulnerability.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Dependabot security updates are merged as soon as CI passes.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Secrets live in GitHub environment secrets; secret scanning and push protection are on.
crypto_published_justification: Bientôt uses only published algorithms through the platform: Windows DPAPI to protect a stored token, TLS from Windows for HTTPS, and SHA-256 for file names and fingerprints that are not security controls.
crypto_call_justification: Bientôt implements no cryptography itself; it calls Windows DPAPI, the Windows TLS stack and the RustCrypto sha2 crate.
crypto_floss_justification: Everything that relies on cryptography (HTTPS, protecting a token at rest) can be implemented with free software such as rustls and libsodium.
crypto_keylength_justification: Bientôt sets no key lengths: Windows manages the DPAPI and TLS keys.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithm is used for security.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No algorithm or mode with known serious weaknesses is used.
crypto_pfs_justification: Bientôt implements no key agreement protocol; HTTPS is handled by Windows.
crypto_password_storage_justification: Bientôt has no user accounts and stores no passwords to authenticate users.
crypto_random_justification: Bientôt generates no cryptographic keys or nonces.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (GitHub default setup) and cargo clippy run on every pull request and push to main.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL looks for common vulnerabilities in the Rust code, the TypeScript web service and the GitHub workflows.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CodeQL findings are fixed or dismissed with a reason; the default branch ruleset blocks merges on high CodeQL alerts.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every pull request and push to main.
dynamic_analysis_justification: cargo-fuzz targets fuzz the settings, transfer and ledger parsers on pull requests that touch them and every week. https://github.com/Thanaen/Bientot/actions/workflows/fuzz.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The code is Rust; the fuzz targets run with AddressSanitizer, the cargo-fuzz default.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Fuzzing failures become regular tests once fixed, as CONTRIBUTING.md asks.
